blocked_on: the sealing tool is single-volume by construction, in three separate ways: seal-content is fixed to the G17b checkpoint and replaces evidence/current/ rather than adding beside it; build-reserve's volume id, checkpoint id and build paths are 0001 constants; and seal-catalog rebuilds the catalog and requires an explicit supersession of the existing set rather than appending an entry. Extending them is a change to the shape of the chain, not a parameter

three design questions belong to the owner and are answered nowhere checkable: whether evidence/current/ means the latest volume or gains a per-volume directory; whether the outer catalog is appended to or superseded and rewritten with two entries; and what volume-0002's checkpoint records as its predecessor_checkpoint_sha256, a field volume-0001 leaves null
budget_finding: all 46 candidates are 714,736,465 bytes and exceed the 650 MiB volume budget by 33,162,065. The 40 without the superseded archives are 611,312,795 and fit with 70,261,605 to spare. So the superseded six are left out of the seal -- which is not the same as deleting them: they stay in the evidence directory, and the reserve holds only archives today's release check accepts.
